message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical, Chemical, and Nuclear Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Symbol** | H | |
| **Standard atomic weight** | 1.00794 u (average of isotopes) | |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H, D), Tritium (^3H, T) | Protium: 99.98 % natural; Deuterium: 0.015 %; Tritium: trace. |
| **Density (STP)** | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ | Lowest density of any element. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (−434.3 °F) | Solidifies only at very low temperatures. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) | Gaseous at room temperature. |
| **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.01588 g mol⁻¹ | |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | Highest among all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ | |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ | |
| **Diffusion coefficient (air, 25 °C)** | ~0.0002 m² s⁻¹ | Extremely high diffusivity. |
| **Magnetic moment (protium)** | 2.792847 µ_N | |
| **Nuclear spin** | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) | |
| **Allotropes** | H₂ (diatomic), H₃⁺ (triatomic cation), H₂O (water), H₂S, etc. | |
| **Physical state at STP** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas | |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (vol/vol) in air | |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂); reacts with halogens (HF, HCl, HBr, HI); reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). | |
| **Solubility in water** | 0.0007 g g⁻¹ (at 25 °C) | Very low solubility. |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant (liquid H₂ + liquid O₂), industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), metal processing, semiconductor manufacturing, etc. | |
| **Abundance** | Most abundant element in the universe (~75 % by mass). | |
| **Nuclear properties** | Deuterium (spin 1) used in nuclear fusion research; Tritium (radioactive, half‑life 12.32 y) used in fusion reactors and radiolabeling. | |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Atomic number 1, lowest density, highest ionization energy.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide range of compounds (hydrides, acids, oxides).
- **Flammable**: Explosive limits in air make it both a powerful energy source and a safety hazard.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive, used in fusion).
- **Industrial importance**: Key feedstock for ammonia, methanol, and many other chemicals; central to hydrogen‑fuel cell technology and rocket propulsion.

These properties make hydrogen unique among the elements, enabling its role as a clean energy carrier, a fundamental building block in chemistry, and a critical component in advanced technologies such as fusion research.
